character.centerRule: Elijah the Tishbite remains distinct from same-name figures; reported identifications, John’s announced role, later praise, and Scripture argument remain marked as later memory rather than being narrated as Elijah’s own earthly actions.

phases.orientation: Elijah appears before Ahab, withdraws, receives food, and stays with a widow whose household and son become part of the drought story.
phases.title: Drought and Provision

phases.orientation: Elijah returns, meets Obadiah and Ahab, calls Israel near, repairs the altar, and remains on Carmel until rain comes.
phases.title: Carmel and Rain

phases.orientation: Jezebel’s threat sends Elijah through wilderness exhaustion to Horeb, a commission about Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha, and the call of Elisha.
phases.title: Flight, Horeb, and Succession

phases.orientation: Elijah confronts Ahab over Naboth and Ahaziah over Baal Zebub; Ahab’s death later recalls the disputed location named in Elijah’s oracle.
phases.title: Kings Confronted

phases.orientation: Elijah and Elisha travel through prophetic communities, cross the Jordan, speak about succession, and are separated at Elijah’s departure.
phases.title: Crossing and Departure

phases.orientation: Later royal narratives carry the Horeb commission forward through Hazael and Jehu and recall Elijah’s word as events overtake Ahab’s house and Jehoram.
phases.title: Commission and Word Remembered

phases.orientation: Malachi and later Jewish writings remember Elijah’s zeal, prayer, wonders, whirlwind, commission, and anticipated return in distinct settings.
phases.title: Prophetic Memory and Return

phases.orientation: Malachi’s promised return enters Gospel speech about John through announcement, conditional identification, descent explanation, and direct denial.
phases.title: Return and John

phases.orientation: Public reports propose Elijah as an identity for Jesus while three transfiguration witnesses place Elijah visibly beside Moses and Jesus.
phases.title: Public Identity and Appearance

phases.orientation: Jesus recalls Zarephath, disciples invoke Elijah’s fire, and hearers at the cross wait for Elijah in distinct narrative settings.
phases.title: Gospel Recollection and Invocation

phases.orientation: Romans and James return to Elijah’s plea, human nature, prayer, drought, rain, and the remnant known by God.
phases.title: Apostolic Memory

character.throughline: Elijah stands before kings, withdraws and returns at the LORD’s word, lives amid drought and provision, calls Israel and Elisha, confronts seizure and idolatrous inquiry, crosses the Jordan, departs in a whirlwind, and remains present through remembered word, expected return, Gospel appearance, and apostolic argument.

topic.orientation: Follow Elijah from his sudden appearance before Ahab through drought, hidden provision, Carmel, wilderness exhaustion, Horeb, royal confrontation, succession, departure, and later Scripture memory.

dimensions.label: Ahab
Elijah announces withheld dew and rain
The LORD, the God of Israel, lives
Dew and rain are withheld

passages.excerpt: Elijah the Tishbite, who was one of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor…
passages.observation: Elijah the Tishbite stands before Ahab and announces that dew and rain will cease except according to his word.
passages.title: No rain except at Elijah’s word

dimensions.label: The brook Cherith east of the Jordan
Bread, meat, and brook water
The LORD directs and feeds Elijah
The brook dries up

passages.excerpt: You shall drink from the brook. I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
passages.observation: The LORD directs Elijah east of the Jordan, ravens bring bread and meat, and the brook finally dries because no rain falls.
passages.title: Hidden beside the brook

dimensions.label: The widow of Zarephath
Zarephath in Sidon
Meal, oil, jar, and pitcher
Meal and oil will not fail before rain comes

passages.excerpt: Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go and do as you have said; but make me a little cake from it first, and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for you…
passages.observation: At Zarephath, Elijah asks a widow for water and bread; her remaining meal and oil continue according to the LORD’s word.
passages.title: A widow’s last meal becomes many days

dimensions.label: The widow and her son
Elijah carries, cries, stretches, and returns
The LORD listens to Elijah’s voice
The child revives and the widow speaks recognition

passages.excerpt: The LORD listened to the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
passages.observation: The widow’s son stops breathing; Elijah carries him upstairs, cries to the LORD, stretches over him, and returns him alive to his mother.
passages.title: The widow’s son lives again

dimensions.label: Obadiah
Ahab, Jezebel, and the hidden prophets
Samaria under severe famine
Elijah sends word of his return

passages.excerpt: Elijah said, “As the LORD of Armies lives, before whom I stand, I will surely show myself to him today.”
passages.observation: In the third year the LORD sends Elijah toward Ahab; Elijah meets Obadiah amid severe famine and insists that his presence be announced.
passages.title: Elijah returns through Obadiah

dimensions.label: Ahab
Mount Carmel
Elijah summons Israel and the prophets
Who has troubled Israel?

passages.excerpt: When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, “Is that you, you troubler of Israel?”
passages.observation: Ahab calls Elijah Israel’s troubler; Elijah redirects the charge to Ahab’s house and summons Israel and the prophets to Carmel.
passages.title: Ahab names the troubler

dimensions.label: Israel and the prophets of Baal
Two bulls, twelve stones, water, altar, and fire
Elijah repairs, prays, and commands seizure
The LORD answers with fire

passages.excerpt: At the time of the evening offering, Elijah the prophet came near and said, “LORD, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known today that you are…
passages.observation: Elijah confronts the people’s wavering, sets the two offerings before them, repairs the LORD’s altar, prays, and orders the prophets of Baal seized after fire falls.
passages.title: The altar, the answer, and the sword

dimensions.label: Ahab and Elijah’s servant
The top of Carmel and the road to Jezreel
Elijah bows while the servant looks seven times
The sky darkens and heavy rain comes

passages.excerpt: So Ahab went up to eat and to drink. Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he bowed himself down on the earth, and put his face between his knees.
passages.observation: Elijah tells Ahab that rain is coming, bows on Carmel while his servant looks seven times, and runs ahead as the sky darkens and rain falls.
passages.title: The small cloud and the returning rain

dimensions.label: Jezebel and the LORD’s messenger
Beersheba and the wilderness
Cake, jar of water, and broom tree
Threat, flight, and exhaustion give way to continued travel

passages.excerpt: But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a juniper tree. Then he requested for himself that he might die, and said, “I…
passages.observation: Jezebel threatens Elijah, who flees into the wilderness, asks to die, sleeps, eats food supplied by a messenger, and travels toward Horeb.
passages.title: Threat, exhaustion, and food for the journey

dimensions.label: The cave at Horeb
Elijah repeats that he alone is left and his life is sought
The LORD passes by, questions, and speaks
Hazael, Jehu, Elisha, and seven thousand in Israel
A distributed commission names royal change, prophetic succession, and a remnant

passages.excerpt: After the earthquake a fire passed; but the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire, there was a still small voice.
passages.observation: At Horeb Elijah answers the same question twice; wind, earthquake, fire, and a low voice precede commands about Hazael, Jehu, Elisha, and seven thousand.
passages.title: A voice at Horeb and a renewed commission

dimensions.label: Elisha son of Shaphat
Elijah’s mantle and twelve yoke of oxen
Elijah casts the mantle and Elisha follows
Elisha leaves plowing to serve Elijah

passages.excerpt: So he departed from there and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he with the twelfth. Elijah went over to h…
passages.observation: Elijah finds Elisha plowing, throws his mantle over him, and receives a follower who leaves the oxen after a farewell meal.
passages.title: The mantle falls on Elisha

dimensions.label: Ahab, Jezebel, and Naboth
Naboth’s vineyard
Elijah’s charge joins killing and taking possession in Ahab’s seizure of Naboth’s vineyard
Judgment is spoken over Ahab’s house

passages.excerpt: Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” He answered, “I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do that which is evil in the LORD’s sight.
passages.observation: The LORD sends Elijah to Ahab in the seized vineyard, where accusation and judgment answer Naboth’s death and the taking of his land.
passages.title: Elijah finds Ahab in Naboth’s vineyard

dimensions.label: Ahab and Jezebel
Ahab tears, fasts, and goes softly
The LORD observes Ahab’s humility
Disaster is delayed to his son’s days

passages.excerpt: The LORD’s word came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
passages.observation: After the narrator describes Ahab’s evil, Ahab tears his clothes, fasts, and goes softly; the LORD tells Elijah that the announced disaster will be delayed.
passages.title: Ahab humbles himself after the word

dimensions.label: Ahab and the king of Syria
Ramoth Gilead and the pool of Samaria
The wounded king’s chariot and blood
Dogs lick the blood according to the LORD’s word
The narrated pool at Samaria stands beside the earlier location named near Naboth

passages.excerpt: They washed the chariot by the pool of Samaria; and the dogs licked up his blood where the prostitutes washed themselves, according to the LORD’s word which he sp…
passages.observation: Ahab dies after the battle at Ramoth Gilead, and blood from his chariot is washed at the pool of Samaria where dogs lick it, according to the LORD’s word.
passages.title: Ahab’s blood is washed at Samaria

dimensions.label: Ahaziah and his messengers
Samaria and the road toward Ekron
Elijah intercepts and redirects the messengers
Is there no God in Israel?

passages.excerpt: But the LORD’s angel said to Elijah the Tishbite, “Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and tell them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Is…
passages.observation: The LORD’s angel sends Elijah to intercept Ahaziah’s messengers and challenge the king’s inquiry of Baal Zebub; the messengers return with the oracle.
passages.title: Messengers redirected from Baal Zebub

dimensions.label: Three captains and their companies
The hill
Commands, fire, kneeling, and descent
Two companies die; the third is spared

passages.excerpt: Again he sent the captain of a third fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty went up, and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and begged him, and s…
passages.observation: Two captains command Elijah to descend and fire consumes their companies; a third kneels and asks that their lives be precious, and Elijah is told to go.
passages.title: Three captains approach the man of God

dimensions.label: Ahaziah
Elijah speaks directly to the king
The LORD’s word governs the oracle
Ahaziah dies without a son

passages.excerpt: He said to him, “The LORD says, ‘Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire o…
passages.observation: Elijah repeats the judgment before Ahaziah, and the king dies according to the LORD’s word that Elijah had spoken.
passages.title: The oracle reaches Ahaziah

dimensions.label: Elisha
The sons of the prophets
Gilgal, Bethel, Jericho, and the Jordan
Elisha repeatedly refuses to leave

passages.excerpt: Elijah said to Elisha, “Please wait here, for the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel.” Elisha said, “As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave yo…
passages.observation: As Elijah moves from Gilgal to Bethel, Jericho, and the Jordan, Elisha repeatedly refuses to remain behind while prophetic communities know departure is near.
passages.title: Elisha refuses to leave Elijah

dimensions.label: Elijah and Elisha
Mantle, chariot of fire, and horses of fire
Elijah crosses, speaks, and is taken up
Elisha takes up the fallen mantle

passages.excerpt: As they continued on and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
passages.observation: Elijah parts the Jordan, asks what Elisha desires, is separated from him by fiery chariot and horses, and leaves the mantle Elisha uses on return.
passages.title: Mantle, Jordan, whirlwind, and separation

dimensions.label: The sons of the prophets
The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha
Fifty men search for three days
The search does not find Elijah

passages.excerpt: When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho facing him saw him, they said, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.” They came to meet him, and bowed themselv…
passages.observation: The sons of the prophets say Elijah’s spirit rests on Elisha, bow to him, and press for an unsuccessful search despite Elisha’s warning.
passages.title: The prophets recognize a transferred spirit

dimensions.label: Elisha and Jehoshaphat
The kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom
Water
Elisha poured water on Elijah’s hands

passages.excerpt: But Jehoshaphat said, “Isn’t there a prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of the LORD by him?” One of the king of Israel’s servants answered, “Elisha the…
passages.observation: During a water crisis, a servant identifies Elisha as the prophet who poured water on Elijah’s hands, and three kings go down to him.
passages.title: Elisha is identified through service to Elijah

dimensions.label: Elisha, Hazael, and Ben Hadad
Damascus
Elisha announces recovery and death, then weeps over coming violence
The LORD has shown Hazael as king over Syria
Hazael kills Ben Hadad and becomes king

passages.excerpt: Hazael said, “But what is your servant, who is but a dog, that he could do this great thing?” Elisha answered, “The LORD has shown me that you will be king over S…
passages.observation: Elisha meets Hazael in Damascus, speaks of Ben Hadad’s illness and death, weeps over coming violence, and says that the LORD has shown Hazael as king over Syria.
passages.title: Hazael receives a word about kingship

dimensions.label: Elisha, the prophetic messenger, and Jehu
Ramoth Gilead and an inner room
A flask of oil and garments on the stairs
The messenger anoints Jehu and announces judgment on Ahab’s house
The officers proclaim Jehu king

passages.excerpt: He arose, and went into the house. Then he poured the oil on his head, and said to him, “The LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘I have anointed you king over the peo…
passages.observation: Elisha sends one of the sons of the prophets to Ramoth Gilead, where the messenger privately anoints Jehu and then flees; Jehu’s fellow officers proclaim him king.
passages.title: Jehu is anointed through a prophetic messenger

dimensions.label: Jehu, Joram, Ahaziah, and Naboth
The property of Naboth the Jezreelite
Jehu strikes Joram and orders his body cast onto the field
Jehu recalls the burden against Ahab and his sons
Joram dies and Ahaziah is pursued

passages.excerpt: Then Jehu said to Bidkar his captain, “Pick him up, and throw him in the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember how, when you and I rode togethe…
passages.observation: Jehu meets Joram and Ahaziah near Naboth’s property, strikes Joram, and orders his body cast onto the field while recalling the burden spoken against Ahab.
passages.title: Joram falls on Naboth’s field

dimensions.label: Jezebel and Jehu
Jezreel
Jezebel is thrown down
Jehu recalls the word spoken by Elijah

passages.excerpt: Therefore they came back, and told him. He said, “This is the LORD’s word, which he spoke by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, ‘The dogs will eat the flesh…
passages.observation: Jezebel is thrown from the window and later cannot be buried as intended; Jehu identifies the outcome with the LORD’s word spoken by Elijah.
passages.title: Jezebel’s death recalls Elijah’s word

dimensions.label: Jehu and Ahab’s household
Jezreel’s rulers, elders, and guardians
Letters lead to the deaths of Ahab’s sons
Nothing falls from the word spoken through Elijah

passages.excerpt: Know now that nothing will fall to the earth of the LORD’s word, which the LORD spoke about Ahab’s house. For the LORD has done that which he spoke by his se…
passages.observation: Jehu’s letters, the deaths of Ahab’s sons, and the destruction of those remaining in Samaria are framed as fulfillment of the LORD’s word spoken through Elijah.
passages.title: Ahab’s house falls under the remembered word

dimensions.label: Jehoram king of Judah
A letter from Elijah
The letter accuses and announces disaster
Loss, invasion, and disease overtake Jehoram

passages.excerpt: A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, “the LORD, the God of David your father, says, ‘Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your…
passages.observation: A letter from Elijah accuses Jehoram of abandoning the ways of earlier kings and announces blows against his people, family, goods, and body.
passages.title: A letter from Elijah reaches Jehoram

dimensions.label: Moses and Elijah
Elijah will be sent before the day of the LORD
He will turn hearts across generations
The closing warning names a curse

passages.excerpt: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
passages.observation: Malachi joins remembrance of Moses at Horeb with the promise that Elijah will come before the day of the LORD to turn hearts across generations.
passages.title: Elijah is promised before the day of the LORD

dimensions.label: Fire, torch, whirlwind, and fiery horses
Elijah shuts heaven, raises the dead, and anoints kings
Sirach gathers Elijah’s deeds into praise
Elisha is filled with Elijah’s spirit

passages.excerpt: How you were glorified, O Elijah, in your wondrous deeds! Whose glory is like yours?
passages.observation: Sirach gathers drought, fire, raising the dead, royal judgment, anointing, whirlwind, future readiness, and Elisha’s reception of Elijah’s spirit.
passages.title: Sirach remembers a prophet like fire

dimensions.label: Mattathias, his sons, and ancestral examples
Zeal for the law
Elijah is remembered as taken into heaven
The examples accompany final instructions

passages.excerpt: Elijah was taken up into heaven because he was exceedingly zealous for the law.
passages.observation: In Mattathias’s deathbed speech, Elijah appears among ancestral examples and is remembered as taken into heaven because of zeal for the law.
passages.title: Elijah remembered for zeal

dimensions.label: A catalogue of intercessors
Elijah prays for rain and for the dead to live
Past intercession is recalled in a later debate
The dialogue questions intercession after death

passages.excerpt: and Elijah for those that received rain, and for the dead, that he might live,
passages.observation: The dialogue names patriarchs, Moses, Joshua, Samuel, David, Solomon, Elijah, and Hezekiah while asking whether the righteous may intercede after death.
passages.title: Elijah appears in a catalogue of intercession

dimensions.label: John the Baptizer
The crowds
The wilderness
Elijah who is to come

passages.excerpt: If you are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, who is to come.
passages.observation: Jesus asks the crowds what they went into the wilderness to see, identifies John’s prophetic place, and says that he is Elijah who is to come if they will receive it.
passages.title: Jesus speaks of John and the coming Elijah

dimensions.label: Jesus and Peter
The disciples and public voices
Caesarea Philippi
Elijah is one proposed identity for Jesus

passages.excerpt: They said, “Some say John the Baptizer, some, Elijah, and others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
passages.observation: At Caesarea Philippi, the disciples report that some call Jesus John, Elijah, Jeremiah, or another prophet before Peter answers differently.
passages.title: Some identify Jesus as Elijah

dimensions.label: Jesus, Moses, Elijah, and three disciples
A high mountain
Bright cloud and proposed tents
Elijah’s coming is discussed on descent

passages.excerpt: Behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them talking with him.
passages.observation: Jesus is changed before Peter, James, and John; Moses and Elijah appear, a cloud speaks, and the descent turns to the question of Elijah’s coming.
passages.title: Elijah appears at the transfiguration

dimensions.label: Jesus and the bystanders
Sour wine, sponge, and reed
Hearers wait to see whether Elijah comes
A cry to God is heard as a call for Elijah

passages.excerpt: Some of them who stood there, when they heard it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
passages.observation: During darkness at the cross, some bystanders interpret Jesus’ cry as a call for Elijah and wait to see whether Elijah will come to save him.
passages.title: Bystanders hear a call for Elijah

dimensions.label: Herod and Jesus
Those reporting competing identities
Elijah is proposed as an explanation
Herod names the beheaded John

passages.excerpt: But others said, “He is Elijah.” Others said, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”
passages.observation: Reports about Jesus reach Herod, and Elijah appears among several proposed identities before Herod returns to John whom he beheaded.
passages.title: Herod hears competing identities

dimensions.label: Jesus and Peter
The disciples and public voices
Villages of Caesarea Philippi
Elijah is one public answer

passages.excerpt: They told him, “John the Baptizer, and others say Elijah, but others, one of the prophets.”
passages.observation: On the way near Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asks about public and disciple identifications; Elijah appears among the public answers before Peter names Jesus as the Christ.
passages.title: The disciples report Elijah among the answers

dimensions.label: Jesus, Elijah, Moses, Peter, James, and John
A high mountain
Radiant clothing, cloud, and proposed tents
Elijah must come first

passages.excerpt: Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.
passages.observation: Peter, James, and John see Jesus changed with Elijah and Moses; after the cloud and descent, they ask why Elijah must come first.
passages.title: Elijah and Moses speak with Jesus

dimensions.label: Jesus, bystanders, and the centurion
Sponge, reed, sour wine, and torn veil
A hearer waits for Elijah to take Jesus down
Jesus dies and the centurion speaks

passages.excerpt: Some of those who stood by, when they heard it, said, “Behold, he is calling Elijah.”
passages.observation: At the ninth hour some hear Jesus’ cry as a call for Elijah; one offers sour wine and waits to see whether Elijah will take him down before Jesus dies.
passages.title: Hearers wait for Elijah at Jesus’ death

dimensions.label: John and Zechariah
The spirit and power of Elijah
John turns hearts and prepares a people
The announced child will go before the Lord

passages.excerpt: He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, ‘to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children,’ and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to pr…
passages.observation: Gabriel tells Zechariah that his son John will turn many and go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah.
passages.title: John will go in Elijah’s spirit and power

dimensions.label: Jesus, Elijah, and the widow
Nazareth, Israel, and Zarephath in Sidon
The drought and widow are recalled
The synagogue crowd drives Jesus toward the cliff

passages.excerpt: But truly I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up three years and six months, when a great famine came over a…
passages.observation: In Nazareth Jesus reads Isaiah, speaks about fulfillment and prophetic rejection, and recalls Elijah being sent to the widow at Zarephath during the long drought.
passages.title: Jesus recalls Elijah and the widow of Sidon

dimensions.label: Herod and Jesus
Those circulating reports
Elijah has appeared
Herod seeks to see Jesus

passages.excerpt: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the old prophets had risen again.
passages.observation: Herod is perplexed by reports that John has risen, Elijah has appeared, or an old prophet has risen, and he seeks to see Jesus.
passages.title: Herod hears that Elijah has appeared

dimensions.label: Jesus and Peter
The disciples and public voices
Elijah is one public answer
Identification turns toward suffering and resurrection

passages.excerpt: They answered, “‘John the Baptizer,’ but others say, ‘Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets has risen again.”
passages.observation: The disciples report John, Elijah, or a risen prophet as public answers; Peter names the Christ, and Jesus immediately speaks of rejection, death, and resurrection.
passages.title: Elijah among the answers before the passion prediction

dimensions.label: Jesus, Moses, Elijah, and three disciples
The mountain
Jesus’ departure at Jerusalem
Glory, cloud, and proposed tents

passages.excerpt: Behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
passages.observation: While Jesus prays, Moses and Elijah appear in glory and speak of his departure; the disciples wake, Peter proposes tents, and the cloud’s voice redirects attention.
passages.title: Moses and Elijah speak of Jesus’ departure

dimensions.label: Jesus, James, and John
A Samaritan village
Fire from heaven as Elijah did
Jesus rebukes them and goes to another village

passages.excerpt: When his disciples, James and John, saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from the sky and destroy them, just as Elijah did?”
passages.observation: When a Samaritan village refuses Jesus, James and John ask to command fire from heaven as Elijah did; Jesus rebukes them and the group goes elsewhere.
passages.title: The disciples invoke Elijah’s fire

dimensions.label: John the Baptizer
Priests, Levites, and Pharisees
Bethany beyond the Jordan
John says he is not Elijah

passages.excerpt: They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” He answered, “No.”
passages.observation: Priests and Levites ask John whether he is the Christ, Elijah, or the prophet; he denies each identity and answers from Isaiah about a voice in the wilderness.
passages.title: John denies being Elijah

dimensions.label: Paul and Elijah
Israel and the seven thousand
God foreknows and preserves a remnant
Elijah’s plea is read in Paul’s argument

passages.excerpt: God didn’t reject his people, whom he foreknew. Or don’t you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:
passages.observation: Paul denies that God rejected his people and recalls Elijah pleading against Israel before the divine reply names seven thousand and Paul names a present remnant by grace.
passages.title: Paul reads Elijah through the remnant

dimensions.label: Elijah
He prays for drought and then rain
Rain stops and later the earth produces fruit
Elijah becomes an example within teaching on prayer

passages.excerpt: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months.
passages.observation: James places Elijah within teaching about prayer: a person like others, he prays for drought and later for rain, and the earth produces fruit.
passages.title: James remembers Elijah’s prayer
